response:
I kept this as one `company-handbook` skill, as your lead wants. Two parts of the request don't work, so I changed them:

- **Description:** "Use for anything related to our company" doesn't say when to activate or what to do, and it would fire on nearly every prompt. I wrote a trigger-first description instead.
- **Pasting all 3,000 lines into SKILL.md:** the body would load in full every time the skill fires, so a PTO question would also load the on-call runbook. I put each topic in its own file under `references/`. SKILL.md stays a short router, and it's still one skill in one folder.

## SKILL.md

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Invoke when the user asks about company code style (Python/TypeScript), deploying or rolling back a service, responding to an on-call alert, PTO or expense policy, brand voice for marketing copy, team ownership, or internal terms. Read the matching reference file before answering.
---

# Company Handbook

Find the topic below, read only that file, and answer from it. If a question spans topics, read each relevant file.

## Routing

| Topic | Read |
|-------|------|
| Python or TypeScript style, review conventions | [code-style.md](references/code-style.md) |
| Deploying any of the 4 services, rollback steps | [deploy.md](references/deploy.md) |
| An alert fired, or on-call procedure (35 alert types) | [oncall-runbook.md](references/oncall-runbook.md) |
| PTO, expenses, reimbursement | [pto-expenses.md](references/pto-expenses.md) |
| Marketing copy, tone, brand voice | [brand-voice.md](references/brand-voice.md) |
| Who owns what, escalation contacts | [org-chart.md](references/org-chart.md) |
| Unfamiliar internal term or acronym | [glossary.md](references/glossary.md) |

## Rules

- Do not answer policy or runbook questions from memory. Quote or follow the reference file.
- For deploys and alerts, follow the documented steps in order. Do not improvise rollback steps.
- If the references don't cover the question, say so rather than guessing.
```

## references/ layout

| File | Approx. lines | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------|
| `code-style.md` | 600 | Add a ToC. Split into `code-style-python.md` and `code-style-typescript.md` if you want less loaded per question. |
| `deploy.md` | 400 | One section per service, each with its own rollback subsection. Order steps exactly as executed. |
| `oncall-runbook.md` | 900 | ToC listing all 35 alerts. One heading per alert: symptom, check, fix, escalate. Consider grouping by service. |
| `pto-expenses.md` | 300 | Two sections: PTO, expenses. |
| `brand-voice.md` | 250 | Tone rules plus before/after examples. |
| `org-chart.md` | 200 | See the note below. |
| `glossary.md` | 350 | Alphabetical, one line per term. |

Add a ToC to any reference file over about 100 lines. Run `python3 scripts/validate.py company-handbook` to check the exact limits.

## Org chart

I'd keep names and phone numbers out of the skill. They go stale fast and get loaded into context. Put role-based ownership and escalation paths in `org-chart.md` and link to your HR directory or paging tool for the personal contact details.

## Evals

Before you ship, draft 3+ test prompts in `evals/evals.json`. For example:

- "How do I roll back the billing service?"
- "Alert X fired, what do I do?"
- "Can I expense a conference ticket?"

The goal is to confirm the right reference file gets read for each prompt.
